title: Concurrency Model Checking
summary: Find concurrency bugs by exhaustively enumerating thread interleavings in a small deterministic model: lost updates, deadlocks, broken invariants and minimal counterexamples.
description: Testing with real threads finds a race only when the scheduler happens to cooperate. Here nothing runs on real threads. Threads are small step machines inside a scheduler you control, so every interleaving can be enumerated. You build the machine and the schedule runner, count interleavings, then write a depth-first checker that finds a lost update, a deadlock and a broken invariant. You make it return the minimal counterexample (shortest, then lexicographically first, so the answer is deterministic), prune repeated states so retry loops terminate, and finish by checking a lock-based structure and a flawed lock-free one. A model shows only what it models: it has no memory reordering, no preemption inside an instruction and a fixed small state limit. A visual stepper for replaying schedules is future work; for now counterexamples are printed as thread-id lists.
outcomes: Model threads as step machines and enumerate every interleaving with a depth-first search.
Detect a lost update, a deadlock and an invariant violation, and return the shortest, lexicographically first counterexample schedule.
Explain what a model check proves (all schedules of this model) and what it does not (real hardware, larger sizes).
